bullets.title: META: AI capex surging to ~$250B in 2027 on 14GW compute doubling; Iris chip in September
bullets.body: META plans to double compute capacity to 14GW by YE27, implying 2027 capex of $200B-$275B (MS model was $175B, Jefferies PT $825 Buy). Prometheus cluster came online July, Iris AI chip (AVGO design, TSMC mfg) launches September. META also investing $13B in 1GW Alberta data center (largest outside US). Capex concerns are a near-term overhang but bulls argue 3.6B DAU flywheel and owned infrastructure justify spend; META stock was down ~3.9% on the news.

bullets.title: AVGO: >$30B multiyear Apple deal secures RF/ASIC position; stock +4.8%
bullets.body: Broadcom signed a >$30B multiyear deal with Apple covering custom silicon and wireless connectivity, more than doubling the 2020 agreement. Deal includes $1.5B capex upgrade at Fort Collins and >15B US-made chips. Analysts see AI silicon ramp ~2029/2030; deal limits QRVO/SWKS from regaining RF share. William Blair views it as validating AVGO's multiyear contract strategy post-GOOGL TPU and Anthropic wins.

bullets.title: Semis/WFE: Citi, Mizuho, Wolfe all raise WFE forecasts; AMAT top pick across shops
bullets.body: WFE estimates converging: Citi models $145B/$200B/$250B for 2026-28; Wolfe raises to $185B/$225B for CY27/28; Mizuho raises to $192B/$221B/$214B. TSMC raised 2026 capex to high end of $52-56B; Samsung announced $1.36T investment through 2040; Micron raised FY26 capex to $27B+ and FY27 to $45B+. Mizuho raises AMAT PT to $650 (from $540, Outperform) and LRCX PT to $400 (from $380, Outperform); Citi and Wolfe also favor AMAT for valuation/DRAM exposure. Optical sub-sector (COHR, FN, LITE) flagged as contrarian long.

bullets.title: MU: Raises US capex plan to >$250B through 2035; $3B ecosystem investment announced
bullets.body: Micron increased US fab investment commitment to >$250B through 2035 (vs. prior $200B), targeting 40% domestic DRAM production. Separately, Micron announced up to $3B strategic investment in the US semiconductor ecosystem including $500M financing to GlobalWafers for a Texas 300mm wafer fab plus a 10-year supply agreement.

bullets.title: ANET: +8% on META 14GW compute story; highest revenue exposure to META among networking names
bullets.body: Arista Networks hit a 52-week high at $184.70 (+78.7% YoY), surging ~8% following Reuters reports on META's compute expansion. Mizuho notes ANET has highest percentage revenue exposure to META among networking peers. META and Google are CIEN's top two customers as well.

bullets.title: CIEN: Raymond James sees 30% pullback as buying opportunity; bull-case $20 EPS in FY28
bullets.body: Raymond James, post-CFO meetings, maintains street-high estimates on CIEN: 30%+ growth in FY27-FY28, TAM doubling to $50B by 2029, backlog reaching $9-12B by FY26-end. Bull case EPS $20 in FY28 vs. Street $14.28. CIEN secured DSP+ win displacing Cisco/Acacia at Amazon. Morgan Stanley, however, rates CIEN Equal-weight, preferring NOK (Top Pick OW, €14 PT) for valuation reasons.

bullets.title: NFLX: Citi cuts PT to $100 (from $115, keeps Buy); Bernstein OW on ads/live sports upside
bullets.body: Citi cut NFLX PT from $115 to $100 (25x vs 28x 2027 EPS) but maintains Buy, seeing ~20x 2027 EPS as compelling. Bernstein keeps Outperform with $100 PT, noting World Cup hurt H1 subscriber adds; upside from ad outperformance and NFL games. Citizens sees potential NFLX acquisition of NBCUniversal post-Comcast spinoff as strategically logical but notes linear TV drag would dampen enthusiasm.

bullets.title: MSFT: GS expects F4Q Azure growth of 40-41% cc; CIO survey flags MSFT as top AI spend beneficiary
bullets.body: Goldman expects Microsoft F4Q Azure growth of 40-41% cc (vs. guidance 39-40%) with 1QFY guidance 40-41% cc vs. Street at 41%. Citi CIO survey (IT budgets +3.3% YoY, AI now #1 priority) identifies MSFT as screening best for AI spend increases alongside AMZN and GOOGL. The Economist separately flags MSFT gaming strategy as 'badly misfired.'

bullets.title: PLTR/MDB/SNOW: Citi Tyler Radke names trio as new top picks for data infra/AI enablement
bullets.body: Citi analyst Tyler Radke designates MDB, SNOW, and PLTR as new top picks in software for data infrastructure and AI enablement. PLTR separately benefits from Rackspace's enterprise AI partnership (30mW AMD-based deployment) though UBS remains Neutral on RXT given $150M 2026 revenue cut and near-term supply constraints.

bullets.title: NOW: GS sees attractive setup at 10-year high short interest; upside scenario 20.5-21.5% cRPO growth
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs highlights ServiceNow as offering attractive risk/reward with short interest at 10-year highs. GS upside scenario for 2Q total cRPO growth is 20.5-21.5% vs. guide/consensus of +19.5% cc. Citi CIO survey, however, flags NOW as potentially at risk from AI spend reallocation.

bullets.title: TOST: GS upgrades to Buy; sees rebound on stronger sales environment and AI-marketing acceleration
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded Toast to Buy after disappointing 2Q guidance, citing improving sales environment, pricing benefits, and acceleration of AI-enabled marketing services. No price target specified in the note.

bullets.title: GEV/ENPH: Oppenheimer sees beat-and-raise potential; 800V architecture next catalyst
bullets.body: Oppenheimer flags GEV and AMSC as having beat-and-raise potential on underappreciated data center power demand and grid expansion; raising 2027 estimates on SHLS for pricing power. ENPH faces regulatory/policy headwinds in Europe and US; Opco trimming 2H26 estimates but would be a buyer after the print. 800V power architecture adoption is the next major catalyst, with tangible pilot announcements expected ~one quarter away.

bullets.title: FSLR: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $245 from $230 on strong onsite power and BESS demand
bullets.body: MS Energy analyst Dave Arcaro raises First Solar PT to $245 (from $230) citing strong onsite power and battery energy storage demand. Also raised PLUG PT to $1.65 from $1.50. BE management rebuttal dismissed scandium shortage concerns, citing 25GW annual supply capacity and multiple sourcing options; Arcaro reaffirms bullish view on BE.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye initiates short with 23% downside; AVGO deal provides offset
bullets.body: Hedgeye initiated Apple as a new short at $313.39 entry with 23% downside target; presentation July 14. This counters the bullish AVGO-AAPL >$30B multiyear silicon deal narrative. Apple also lost its EU challenge to 'gatekeeper' status per ESG press digest.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: PSKY downgraded to Sell ($2 PT) at Arete; states may sue to block merger
bullets.body: Arete Research downgraded Paramount (PSKY) to Sell with $2 PT, citing regulatory risk and ~$80B combined debt post-merger. California-led states are preparing to sue to block the PSKY-WBD deal; closing date pushed to at least July 22 pending Oregon AG review.

bullets.title: SNAP/PINS: Initiation divergence — PINS Buy on ARPU growth, SNAP Neutral on engagement/margin headwinds
bullets.body: An analyst initiates PINS at Buy (~10x EBITDA, target 12x minimum) citing 10 straight quarters of LDD user growth and Performance+ SMB tool scaling with new CBO. SNAP initiated at Neutral: NA DAUs down 7% YoY, ad revenue only +3% YoY, hardware (Specs) dragging margins, and ~20% of MAUs are U18 creating regulatory risk; fair multiple 7-8x EBITDA until improvements materialize.

bullets.title: NET: 52-week high at $273.70, +41.9% YoY
bullets.body: Cloudflare hit a new 52-week high at $273.70 (+0.1% on the day, +41.9% over 52 weeks) per StreetAccount screening. No new fundamental catalyst cited in today's flow.

bullets.title: MMYT: JPMorgan raises PT to $65 from $60 in India Internet preview
bullets.body: JPMorgan raises MakeMyTrip PT to $65 from $60 as part of India Internet 1QFY27 preview. Revenue growth expected at 14% YoY with Air segment up only 6% due to Middle East conflict headwinds. MMYT ranked 6th in JPM's sector preference, below Eternal, Meesho, Groww, INFOE, and Swiggy.

bullets.title: META AI pricing & token economics: Muse Spark at $1.25-$4.25/M tokens; enterprise token optimization wave underway
bullets.body: META released Muse Spark 1.1 API at $1.25/$4.25 per M input/output tokens. SpaceX's Grok 4.5 launched at $2/$6/M tokens vs OpenAI GPT 5.5 at $5/$30. Enterprise firms are now capping AI usage and routing workloads to cheaper/open-source models since May, with daily token purchases up 8-12x Jan-May but spend up only 3-4x — a 'tokenmaxx' optimization trend that could reshape the AI story in 2H26.
